translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Thursday, Parshat Yitro,
the fifteenth of Shevat, 5734*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the verse "on this day" regarding the giving of the Torah, Rashi's interpretation that Torah should always be new, and the question of how this is possible after thousands of years.

translations.translation: "In the third month of the children of Israel's going out of the land of Egypt, on this day they came to the Sinai desert."
And it is brought in the Gemara:
It is written here "on this day they came to the Sinai desert" and it is written there,
"This month is for you the beginning of months."
Just as there it is Rosh Chodesh, so too here it is Rosh Chodesh.
And the precise point is known,
that it says "on this day" without specification
(and it is necessary to learn from a gezeirah shavah that it is Rosh Chodesh),
and it does not say "on the first of the month."
And behold, Rashi explains that what is written "on this day"
is that the words of Torah should be new to you, as if they were given today.
And it needs to be understood,
for the simple explanation of "on this day" is that "on this day" refers to Rosh Chodesh Sivan,
but according to the explanation that the words of Torah should be new to you, etc., "on this day" refers to every day of all the days of the year.
Also, it needs to be understood
(as is the precise point in several discourses),
how is it possible for the words of Torah to be new every day, and certainly new, after the Torah was already given more than three thousand years ago?
And seemingly, it is possible to explain this based on what is explained in the discourses on the verse "Zeh"
in the explanation of the verse,
"And Elokim spoke all these words, saying,"
that the word "leimor" (saying) in this verse means that the study of Torah
("all these words")
should be in a manner of "leimor,"
to repeat the words that the Holy One, blessed be He, is saying now,
as it is written,
"My tongue will answer Your word,"
that the Torah is Your word, but my tongue answers like one who answers after the speaker.
And therefore, just as there it was with awe and fear, etc., so too here, etc.,
for when he studies the Torah now, the Holy One, blessed be He, is saying these words now,
in that exact same manner as at the time of the giving of the Torah.
And this also requires explanation,
for since the words of the Holy One, blessed be He, are living and enduring forever without any change,
what is added and renewed by His saying them now
(at the time of a person's study)
once again?

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Midrashic parable of the king nullifying the decree separating heaven and earth at the giving of the Torah, and how this enables mitzvos and Torah study to affect the world and unite with G-d.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what is brought in the Midrash:
A parable of a king who decreed and said: The residents of Rome shall not go down to Syria, and the residents of Syria shall not go up to Rome.
So too, when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He decreed and said: "The heavens are the heavens of Hashem, and the earth He gave to the children of man."
When He desired to give the Torah, He nullified the decree and said: The lower ones shall ascend to the upper ones, and the upper ones shall descend to the lower ones,
and I will begin,
as it is stated,
"And Hashem descended upon Mount Sinai," and it is written,
"And to Moshe He said, 'Ascend to Hashem.'"
And behold, it is known that the revelation of G-dliness in the world that was at the time of the giving of the Torah
(the descent of the upper ones to the lower ones,
"and Hashem descended upon Mount Sinai")
was in a manner from above to below,
meaning that the revelation was from the side of the drawing down from above, and the lower realm was not a vessel for this.
And the matter of "the lower ones shall ascend to the upper ones" is
that at the giving of the Torah, the power was given that the service of Torah and mitzvos after the giving of the Torah will affect the world so that it becomes a vessel for G-dliness.
And as explained elsewhere,
that this—that through the fulfillment of mitzvos, clarification and refinement are made in the things of the world in which the mitzvah is performed—
to the extent that in several matters they become
(the things of the world)
the actual object of the mitzvah,
is through a special power that was given at the giving of the Torah.
For since the mitzvos
(the will of the Holy One, blessed be He)
and the things of the world
(in which the mitzvos are performed)
are completely incomparable,
therefore,
in order for the mitzvos to effect a change in the things of the world, it is specifically through the nullification of the decree and the partition between the upper ones
(mitzvos)
and the lower ones
(the things of the world).
And similarly, regarding the study of Torah,
that this—that through the study of Torah a change is made
(elevation)
in the person who studies it,
to the extent that he becomes united with the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He—
is through the fact that at the giving of the Torah, the nullification of the decree and the partition between the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He
(upper ones)
and the intellect of man
(lower ones) was made.
